analysis.title: The Flow That Mattered Nov 16-20th: A weekend at the Rink
key_insights: EM Asia ex-China saw foreign net selling of US$7.4bn w/w, driven by Taiwan (-US$6.0bn) and Korea (-US$3.9bn), partly offset by India (+US$2.7bn).
Non-Asia EMs saw net buying of US$0.2bn w/w, led by Brazil (+US$0.1bn) and the UAE (+US$0.1bn).
Southbound flows were +US$2.1bn on the week (ytd +US$55bn). Top bought were Tencent, Semi Manufacturing and Meituan, top sold were Baba, Tracker Fund of HK and BOC HK.
Retail buying in Taiwan (+US$2.5bn) and Korea (+US$1.7bn) this week, with US$90bn of retail inflows into Asian markets ytd.
Asia fundamental L/S managers are down 1.6% mtd (ytd 12.4%). Net leverage fell 47.4 points m/m to 10%, the lowest in records of over a decade, amid the recent equity selloff.
Global Prime book continued to see large net selling, with Taiwan and Korea dominating the selling flows.
Net allocation in Korea fell to 2.3% (11th percentile 1-year) and Taiwan to 4.4% (24th percentile 1-year). Asia allocations remain significantly overweight vs benchmarks, versus 20% OW in mid-June.
InfoTech is still the most overweight regional sector at 10.3% OW, down from a ~22% peak in June. Financials is the most underweight.

Prelim October EPFR data shows EM funds most OW Brazil and Mexico and most UW Taiwan. Funds raised exposure most in Thailand and trimmed most in Taiwan, and cut China Industrials and Taiwan Semis most over 1 and 3 months.

sector_views.rationale: Still the most overweight sector in the region at 10.3% OW, down from a ~22% peak in June, as hedge funds de-risk.
Identified as the most underweight sector in the region by hedge fund positioning.

risk_factors: Continued heavy net selling in Taiwan and Korea by foreign investors.
Further de-risking from Asia hedge funds after record-low net leverage, amid the recent equity selloff.
Fund cuts to Taiwan Semis and China Industrials may continue.
